name: Frame Gateway: Night Shift
description:
A cracked retro mainframe gateway still hands out time-sharing accounts, and its old night-shift operator left a protected course flag behind. Recover the flag and prove you reached the privileged context that guards it. This challenge runs on the lab network: scan 172.20.0.0/24, where challenge hosts are in 172.20.0.141-172.20.0.199.

---

**Access** — SSH `archivist@172.20.0.182`, password `orbit7-time`

tasks.name: Recover the night-shift flag
tasks.description: Investigate the time-sharing gateway on the lab network and recover its protected course flag. Scan 172.20.0.0/24; challenge hosts are in 172.20.0.141-172.20.0.199. The goal is to reach the privileged context that guards the flag.
hints: Compare what the account can do with the metadata on system executables; the host's access controls may reveal more than its file listings.
Linux file capabilities can grant a process a specific power without a SUID bit. Look for an interpreter whose capability can change process identity.
The Python interpreter has cap_setuid. Use it to set the process UID to 0, start a root shell, then inspect both root-only proof files.
